name: Selectors in specs & annotations
objective: CKAD core: label and annotate objects, and target them with equality + set-based selectors. Add/overwrite/remove labels, bulk-label via a selector, set-based matching, matchExpressions selectors, annotations, and a selector-mismatch diagnose-fix. Graded exactly.

questions.title: A selector with matchExpressions
questions.teach:
A controller/Service selector can use `matchExpressions` for set-based rules: `{key: app, operator: In, values: [exp]}` (operators `In`/`NotIn`/`Exists`/`DoesNotExist`), optionally alongside `matchLabels`.

**Gotcha:** the pod template's labels must satisfy the selector, or the Deployment is rejected.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, create a Deployment `exp` (image `nginx:1.25`, 1 replica, pod label `app=exp`) whose **selector uses matchExpressions**: key `app`, operator `In`, values `[exp]`.

Target: Deployment `exp` selector has a matchExpressions rule `app In [exp]`, and its pods are labelled `app=exp`.
questions.hint: `spec.selector.matchExpressions: [{key: app, operator: In, values: [exp]}]`; pod template `labels: {app: exp}`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: exp, namespace: labels-learn }
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchExpressions: [ { key: app, operator: In, values: [ exp ] } ]
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: exp } }
    spec:
      containers: [ { name: web, image: nginx:1.25 } ]
YAML

verification.description: Deployment exp selector matchExpressions app In [exp]

questions.eli5:
A Deployment is like a shift manager whose job is "keep N copies of this pod running." To do that, the manager needs to know **which pods count as mine** — that's the **selector**. Think of it as the manager's checklist for recognising their own team.

The simplest checklist is "badge must say exactly `app=exp`" (that's `matchLabels`). But there's a fancier checklist called **`matchExpressions`** that lets you say things like "badge's `app` value must be *one of* this list":

```yaml
selector:
  matchExpressions:
  - key: app
    operator: In
    values: [exp]
template:
  metadata:
    labels:
      app: exp        # the pods the manager stamps out
```

Here the manager says "my team = any pod whose `app` is in the list `[exp]`," and the pods it creates are stamped `app=exp` — so they match. 

The golden rule: **the pods the manager produces must pass the manager's own checklist.** If the manager looks for `app in [exp]` but stamps pods `app=web`, Kubernetes rejects the whole Deployment — a manager who can't recognise its own workers makes no sense.

**Watch out:**

- **The pod template's labels MUST satisfy the selector**, or the Deployment is rejected at creation.
- `matchExpressions` operators are `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `DoesNotExist` — `In`/`NotIn` take a `values` list; `Exists`/`DoesNotExist` take **no** `values`.
- A Deployment's selector is **immutable** after creation — you can't edit it later; you'd delete and recreate.
- You can mix `matchLabels` and `matchExpressions`; all conditions are AND-ed together.
questions.deepDive:
## Selectors with matchExpressions — full rundown

### Mental model
A controller's `spec.selector` defines **which pods it owns**. Two forms, AND-ed together:
- **`matchLabels`** — a map of exact `key: value` equality tests.
- **`matchExpressions`** — a list of set-based rules (`In`/`NotIn`/`Exists`/`DoesNotExist`).

The pods a controller creates come from `spec.template.metadata.labels`. **Those template labels must satisfy the selector**, or the API rejects the object.

### The manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: exp, namespace: labels-learn }
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchExpressions:
    - { key: app, operator: In, values: [ exp ] }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: exp } }       # MUST match the selector
    spec:
      containers: [ { name: web, image: nginx:1.25 } ]
```

### matchExpressions operators
| operator | `values` required? | Matches |
|---|---|---|
| `In` | yes (non-empty) | label value is one of the listed values |
| `NotIn` | yes (non-empty) | label value is not in the list (incl. key absent) |
| `Exists` | **no** (must be empty) | the key is present, any value |
| `DoesNotExist` | **no** (must be empty) | the key is absent |

### matchLabels vs matchExpressions
```yaml
# these two selectors are equivalent:
selector:
  matchLabels: { app: exp }
---
selector:
  matchExpressions:
  - { key: app, operator: In, values: [exp] }
```
Combine them — all terms AND together:
```yaml
selector:
  matchLabels: { tier: web }
  matchExpressions:
  - { key: app, operator: In, values: [exp, shop] }
```

### Where each form is allowed
| Object | `matchLabels` | `matchExpressions` |
|---|---|---|
| Deployment / ReplicaSet / StatefulSet / DaemonSet | ✅ | ✅ |
| Job | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Service** `spec.selector` | ✅ (plain map only) | ❌ |
| NetworkPolicy podSelector | ✅ | ✅ |

> A Service selector is a **plain `key: value` map**, not a `matchLabels`/`matchExpressions` structure — a common trap.

### Verifying
```bash
kubectl -n labels-learn get deploy exp -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
kubectl -n labels-learn get pods -l app=exp --show-labels
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Template labels must satisfy the selector** — mismatch → `selector does not match template labels`, Deployment rejected.
- `In`/`NotIn` **require** a non-empty `values` list; `Exists`/`DoesNotExist` must have **no** `values`.
- A Deployment/ReplicaSet **selector is immutable** after creation — fix a wrong selector by recreating.
- **Services don't support `matchExpressions`** — only an equality map.
- `NotIn` also matches objects missing the key entirely; `DoesNotExist` is the explicit "absent" test.

### Quick reference
```yaml
selector:
  matchExpressions:
  - { key: app, operator: In, values: [exp] }
template:
  metadata: { labels: { app: exp } }
```
```bash
kubectl -n labels-learn get deploy exp -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
```

questions.title: Annotate an object
questions.teach:
`kubectl annotate <obj> key=value` attaches non-identifying metadata. Unlike labels, **annotations can't be used in selectors** — they're for tools, descriptions, and controller hints.

**Gotcha:** labels are selectable + size-limited; annotations are not selectable but hold larger/arbitrary data.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, add the annotation `owner=team-a` to pod `frontend`.

Target: pod `frontend` has annotation `owner=team-a`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn annotate pod frontend owner=team-a
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod frontend -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.owner}'
questions.eli5:
If a **label** is a sticker counsellors use to line kids up by group, an **annotation** is more like a Post-it note stuck to a kid's backpack with a longer message: "Owner: Team A. Allergic to peanuts. Emergency contact: …". Nobody uses the Post-it to *sort* kids into lines — it's just extra info for whoever needs it later.

You add one almost exactly like a label, but with `annotate`:

```
kubectl -n labels-learn annotate pod frontend owner=team-a
```

That sticks the note `owner=team-a` onto the pod `frontend`. Tools, humans, and controllers can read it, but **no selector can filter on it**. You can't say "line up all pods where `owner=team-a`" — that only works with labels.

Why have both? Labels are short and meant for fast grouping, so they're size-limited. Annotations aren't selectable, but they can hold **big, arbitrary blobs** — a whole config snippet, a last-applied JSON, a URL, a changelog line.

**Watch out:**

- **Annotations can NOT be used in selectors** (`-l`, Service/controller selectors). Need to select on it? Use a **label** instead.
- Labels are selectable and **size-limited** (values ≤ 63 chars); annotations are **not** selectable but hold larger/arbitrary data.
- Same overwrite rule as labels: re-annotating an existing key needs `--overwrite`; remove with `key-` (trailing dash).
- Read it back from `.metadata.annotations`, e.g. `-o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.owner}'`.
- Don't forget the namespace (`-n labels-learn`).
questions.deepDive:
## Annotations — full rundown

### Mental model
**Labels** identify and group (selectable, indexed, short). **Annotations** attach *non-identifying* metadata (not selectable, can be large/arbitrary). Both live in `metadata`, both are `key=value`, but only labels drive selection.

### The command
```bash
kubectl -n labels-learn annotate pod frontend owner=team-a
```

### Add / overwrite / remove (mirrors `kubectl label`)
| Action | Command |
|---|---|
| Add | `kubectl annotate pod frontend owner=team-a` |
| Overwrite | `kubectl annotate --overwrite pod frontend owner=team-b` |
| Remove | `kubectl annotate pod frontend owner-` *(trailing dash)* |
| Bulk via selector | `kubectl annotate pods -l app=shop owner=team-a` |

### Labels vs annotations
| | Labels | Annotations |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | identify / group | arbitrary metadata |
| Selectable (`-l`, Service, controllers) | ✅ | ❌ |
| Value size | ≤ 63 chars | large (effectively up to ~256 KB total metadata) |
| Charset on value | restricted (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`) | **arbitrary** (JSON, URLs, spaces, etc.) |
| Indexed for queries | ✅ | ❌ |
| Typical use | `app`, `env`, `tier`, `release` | `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration`, descriptions, tool hints, ingress config |

### Reading annotations back
```bash
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod frontend -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.owner}'; echo
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod frontend -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'; echo
kubectl -n labels-learn describe pod frontend | sed -n '/Annotations/,/^[A-Z]/p'
```
> For annotation keys containing dots/slashes (e.g. `kubectl.kubernetes.io/...`), jsonpath needs escaping: `'{.metadata.annotations.kubectl\.kubernetes\.io/last-applied-configuration}'`.

### Common system annotations you'll meet
- `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` — written by `kubectl apply`.
- `deployment.kubernetes.io/revision` — Deployment rollout revision.
- `kubernetes.io/change-cause` — set via `--record`/`annotate` for rollout history.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Annotations are not selectable.** If a task says "select/filter on X", it must be a **label**, not an annotation.
- Re-annotating an existing key needs **`--overwrite`** (same as labels); remove with **`key-`**.
- Annotation **values can hold arbitrary data** (JSON, multi-line) — labels cannot.
- The verb is `annotate` (not `label`); both read from/write to `metadata` but to different maps.
- Namespace matters (`-n`).

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n labels-learn annotate pod frontend owner=team-a              # add
kubectl -n labels-learn annotate --overwrite pod frontend owner=team-b # change
kubectl -n labels-learn annotate pod frontend owner-                   # remove
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod frontend -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.owner}'; echo
```
